title: Deloitte NLA style · MCQ + Coding
description: Language, aptitude and technical MCQs with two coding problems. 65 MCQs + 2 coding problems in 90 minutes. Original practice questions modelled on the publicly reported test pattern. Not an official or past paper.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Remote work was once rare in Indian companies. The pandemic forced firms to try it at scale, and many found that productivity did not fall. Employees saved hours of commuting, and companies saved on office space. However, new problems appeared: junior staff missed informal learning from seniors, and some people found it hard to separate work from home life. Many firms have now settled on a hybrid model, with two or three office days a week.

Which problem of remote work does the passage mention?
options: Juniors missed informal learning from seniors
questions.explanation: The passage supports: Juniors missed informal learning from seniors.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The manager gave his ____ to the proposal.
questions.explanation: Correct: The manager gave his consent to the proposal.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) The teacher (B) as well as the students (C) were present (D) at the function.
questions.explanation: Subject is ‘the teacher’: ‘was present’.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘MUNDANE’.
questions.explanation: ‘mundane’ means ordinary.

questions.text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to ‘CANDID’.
questions.explanation: ‘candid’ means frank; its opposite is ‘deceptive’.

questions.text: Choose the best replacement for the part in brackets: I prefer reading [than] watching TV.
questions.explanation: Correct: I prefer reading to watching TV.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Electric vehicles are becoming more common in Indian cities. They produce no exhaust and are cheaper to run than petrol vehicles. Their main drawbacks are a higher purchase price and a shortage of charging stations. As battery prices fall and more chargers are installed, experts expect electric two-wheelers and buses to spread fastest.

Which is an advantage of electric vehicles mentioned in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage supports: Lower running cost.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The new policy will come ____ effect next month.
questions.explanation: Correct: The new policy will come into effect next month.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) I (B) will call you (C) when I will reach (D) home.
questions.explanation: Time clause takes the present: ‘when I reach’.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘ACQUIESCE’.
questions.explanation: ‘acquiesce’ means agree.

questions.text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to ‘IMPARTIAL’.
questions.explanation: ‘impartial’ means fair; its opposite is ‘biased’.

questions.text: Choose the best replacement for the part in brackets: [Being a rainy day], we stayed at home.
options: As it was a rainy day
questions.explanation: Correct: As it was a rainy day, we stayed at home.

questions.text:

Public libraries are changing. Besides books, many now offer free internet, study spaces and workshops on coding or job skills. For students who lack a quiet place at home, the library becomes a second classroom. Libraries that adapted in this way have seen visitor numbers rise even as reading habits shift online.

For some students the library becomes
questions.explanation: The passage supports: a second classroom.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: I wish I ____ more time to prepare.
questions.explanation: Correct: I wish I had more time to prepare.

questions.text: Choose the word closest in meaning to ‘AUGMENT’.
questions.explanation: ‘augment’ means increase.

questions.text: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to ‘OBSOLETE’.
questions.explanation: ‘obsolete’ means outdated; its opposite is ‘modern’.

questions.text:
Read the passage and answer.

Good sleep is essential for learning. While we sleep, the brain sorts and stores what we learned during the day. Students who stay up all night before an exam often remember less than those who sleep well, even if they studied for more hours. Regular sleep times, less screen use before bed and a dark, quiet room all improve sleep quality.

The main idea of the passage is that
questions.explanation: The passage supports: sleep supports learning.

questions.text: Fill in the blank: The report must be submitted ____ Friday.
questions.explanation: Correct: The report must be submitted by Friday.

questions.text:
Spot the part of the sentence that has an error:
(A) Mathematics (B) are (C) my favourite (D) subject.
questions.explanation: ‘Mathematics’ is singular: ‘is’.

questions.text: Rs 5950 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 4 : 7 : 6. What is C's share?
Rs 5400 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is C's share?
What is the area of a circle of radius 21 cm? (Use π = 22/7)
Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 30 and 12 hours. Pipe C can empty it in 15 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/30 + 1/12 − 1/15 = 1/20 tank/hour, so 20 hours.

questions.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 30 and 20 hours. Pipe C can empty it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will the tank take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/30 + 1/20 − 1/20 = 1/30 tank/hour, so 30 hours.

questions.text: What is 65% of 600?
The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5:4. After 6 years, the ratio will be 6:5. What is A's present age?
questions.explanation: Let ages be 5x and 4x. (5x+6)/(4x+6) = 6/5 gives x = 6; A = 30.

questions.text: What is the compound interest on Rs 10000 at 20% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
A boat's speed in still water is 20 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long will it take to go 782 km upstream and come back?
questions.explanation: Upstream 46 h at 17 km/h, downstream 34 h at 23 km/h; total 80 h.

questions.text: What is the compound interest on Rs 8000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
A can do a job in 36 days and B in 4 days. They work together for 2 days, then B leaves. In how many more days will A finish the job?
questions.explanation: In 2 days they do 5/9 of the work; 4/9 is left, which A does in 4/9 × 36 = 16 days.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 250 m and 300 m run at 72 km/h and 18 km/h in opposite directions. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s; distance = 550 m; time = 22 s.

questions.text: What is 45% of 600?
3 bells ring at intervals of 4, 24 and 9 seconds. If they ring together now, after how many seconds will they next ring together?
questions.explanation: LCM(4, 24, 9) = 72 seconds.

questions.text: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the stream flows at 5 km/h. How long will it take to go 15 km upstream and come back?
questions.explanation: Upstream 3 h at 5 km/h, downstream 1 h at 15 km/h; total 4 h.

questions.text: What comes next: DW, FU, HS, JQ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2; second letters move −2 from the other end of the alphabet.

questions.text: What comes next: BY, FU, JQ, NM, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4; second letters move −4 from the other end of the alphabet.

questions.text: What comes next in the series: 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, ?
questions.explanation: Rule: multiply by 2 each time. Next term = 192.
The rule is n → 2n + 3; for 2 it gives 7.

questions.text: What comes next: BY, DW, FU, HS, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2; second letters move −2 from the other end of the alphabet.

questions.text: In a certain code, PLANET is written as QMBOFU. How is SILVER written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted +1 place in the alphabet.

questions.text: What comes next in the series: 2, 7, 17, 37, 77, ?
questions.explanation: Rule: multiply by 2 and add 3. Next term = 157.

questions.text: Which number is the odd one out: 53, 11, 43, 49?
questions.explanation: 49 — all others are prime.

questions.text: In a row of 28 students, Rahul is 18th from the left. Meera is 3 places to the right of Rahul. What is Meera's position from the right end?
questions.explanation: Meera is 21st from the left, so 28 − 21 + 1 = 8th from the right.
The rule is n → n² + n; for 7 it gives 56.

questions.text: A man is facing West. He turns left, then turns about. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Right = 90° clockwise, left = 90° anticlockwise, about = 180°. Final direction: North.

questions.text: Zoya is taller than Farhan. Tarun is taller than Uma. Uma is taller than Zoya. Gita is taller than Tarun. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation: Chaining the clues: Gita > Tarun > Uma > Zoya > Farhan. The second tallest is Tarun.
a ⊕ b = a² + b²; so 5 ⊕ 4 = 41.

questions.text: Chitra is the son of Sneha. Sneha is the sister of Bharat. Bharat is the father of Gita. How is Chitra related to Gita?
questions.explanation: Chitra's mother and Gita's father are siblings, so they are cousins.

questions.text: What does the ‘static’ keyword on a Java method mean?

It belongs to the class, not to an object
questions.explanation: Static members are shared at class level.

questions.text: Which loop in C always runs its body at least once?
questions.explanation: The condition is checked after the body.

questions.explanation: Standard input/output.

questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles state and behaviour.

questions.text: Keys are inserted into an empty BST in this order: 9, 1, 8, 40, 65, 3, 11, 63. What is the height of the tree (number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path)?
questions.explanation: The longest path has 4 nodes.

questions.text:
What is the output? (div = integer division)

n = 4679
s = 0
while n > 0
    s = s + (n mod 10)
    n = n div 10
end while
print s
questions.explanation: Trace the loop digit by digit.

questions.text: Keys are inserted into an empty binary search tree in this order: 66, 42, 5, 2, 82, 16, 25, 86. What is the preorder traversal?
questions.explanation: Build the BST, then visit root, left subtree, right subtree.

questions.text: Keys are inserted into an empty BST in this order: 14, 21, 27, 68, 3, 76. What is the height of the tree (number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path)?
questions.explanation: The longest path has 5 nodes.

questions.text:
What is the time complexity of this code?

for i = 1 to n
    j = 1
    while j < n
        j = j * 2
questions.explanation: Count how many times the innermost statement runs: O(n log n).

questions.text:
Read a string and print YES if it reads the same forwards and backwards ignoring case and non-letter characters, otherwise NO.

Input: one line (at most 10^5 characters).
Output: YES or NO.

starterCode.python:
import sys

text = sys.stdin.read()
# write your code here
starterCode.javascript:

questions.title: Maximum subarray sum
questions.text:
Given n integers, print the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray.

Input: first line n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5); second line n integers (−10^4 to 10^4).
Output: the maximum subarray sum.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
# write your code here
starterCode.javascript:
const data = require('fs').readFileSync(0, 'utf8').trim().split(/\s+/);
// write your code here

questions.explanation: Reference approach: see the standard technique for ‘Maximum subarray sum’.
